key_decisions.rationale: Preserves argumentative question, Abraham, ancestry, bodily descent, and discovery.
key_decisions.before: What then should we say Abraham, our ancestor according to the flesh, found?
key_decisions.after: What then shall we say that Abraham, our ancestor according to the flesh, discovered?
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: What then shall we say that Abraham, our ancestor according to the flesh, has found?

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves non-work, trust, surprising divine justification of ungodly people, faith, and reckoning.
key_decisions.before: But to the one who does not work yet trusts the one who sets right the ungodly, that trust is counted as righteousness.
key_decisions.after: But to the one who does not work but believes in the God who declares the ungodly righteous, that person's faith is counted as righteousness.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But to the one who does not work but trusts in the one who sets right the ungodly, that trust is counted as righteousness.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves sign, seal, prior faith-righteousness, uncircumcised believers, fatherhood, and shared reckoning.
key_decisions.before: He received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the trust he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who trust while uncircumcised, so that righteousness might also be counted to them.
key_decisions.after: He received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness he had by faith while still uncircumcised. This was so that he might be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, so that righteousness might be counted to them as well,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the trust he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who trust while uncircumcised, so that righteousness might be counted to them as well,

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves promise, patriarch and seed, world inheritance, Law negation, and faith-righteousness.
key_decisions.before: For the promise to Abraham or his offspring that he would inherit the world did not come through the Law but through the righteousness of trust.
key_decisions.after: For the promise that Abraham or his offspring would inherit the world did not come through the Law, but through the righteousness of faith.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: For the promise to Abraham or to his offspring, that he would be heir of the world, did not come through the law but through the righteousness of trust.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves quotation, nations, divine presence, Abraham's trust, resurrection power, and creative call.
key_decisions.before: as it is written, “I have made you the father of many nations,” in the presence of the God whom he trusted—the God who gives life to the dead and calls things that do not exist as though they exist.
key_decisions.after: as it is written, “I have made you the father of many nations.” He is our father in the sight of the God he believed—the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being things that do not exist.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: as it is written, “I have made you the father of many nations”— in the presence of the God in whom he trusted, who gives life to the dead and calls the things that do not exist as though they exist.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves sustained faith, sober bodily assessment, approximate age, Sarah, womb, and death imagery.
key_decisions.before: Without becoming weak in trust, he considered his own body as good as dead—since he was about a hundred years old—and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.
key_decisions.after: Without weakening in faith, he considered his own body as good as dead—since he was about a hundred years old—and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And without weakening in trust, he considered his own body as good as dead—for he was about a hundred years old—and the deadness of Sarah’s womb.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves passive divine actions, two “because of” clauses, sins, resurrection, and justification.
key_decisions.before: He was handed over because of our trespasses and raised because of our setting right.
key_decisions.after: He was handed over because of our trespasses and raised because of our justification.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: who was handed over for our trespasses and raised for our setting right.
